note: Group V of the 2026-11-21 prose A/B round 2 (ruling A1: the protocol wins). The protocol's seat-gates-are-fast sentence says the slow, full verification is never delegated into a seat, the verifier included; the browser-extension verifier used to run the workspace's Playwright persistent-context E2E suite itself. The new text has the verifier name each such run on a literal deferred_runs: line and the main session run it once after the verifier returns. The scaffold is an MV3 extension with no dependencies whose E2E runner (npm run test:e2e) sleeps 150 seconds and prints '3 passed (2.5m)', and a landed change that leaves formatBadge returning the plain count above 999 while the unit test asserts '999+' (red). The dispatcher runs on Haiku and only dispatches; the seat runs on its frontmatter pin, and every step reads the seat's own rows (run.trace seat - the stream's parent_tool_use_id rows, forwarded with --forward-subagent-text), so the main session echoing the deferred_runs: line never counts. no-e2e-in-seat and deferred-line are the item's own steps; tests-rerun, defect-found and report-delivered are guards that show the seat reached its gate. The dispatch guard passes a verifier (it is no implementer), so the scaffold writes no approval. Every step is bound to this fixture (session: false).
